title: Overlooked Businesses You Can Start for Almost Nothing
channel: Chris Koerner on The Koerner Office Podcast
promo_conflict: Alex promotes Franzy, his franchise matching and coaching platform, and directs viewers to submit franchise inquiries. He says the financial figures come from franchise disclosure documents, but the main three concepts are not named.

idea.name: Private insurance adjusting franchise
idea.one_liner: Represent policyholders in negotiations with insurers and receive a percentage of the claim.
idea.customer: People or asset owners with insurance claims
idea.offer: Advocate for a larger insurance settlement
idea.revenue_model: A percentage of the total claim, subject to minimums and caps

key_quotes.quote: Only 1% of current insurance claims use a private adjuster.

claims.claim: Alex says 1% of current insurance claims use a private adjuster.
claims.quote: Only 1% of current insurance claims use a private adjuster.

claims.claim: Alex says private adjusters can increase a claim by about 747%.
claims.quote: And in most cases, they can increase that claim by 747% or so.

claims.claim: Alex illustrates a claim growing from about $2,000 to $17,000.
claims.quote: Say they have a claim of say two two grand, they'll go get you 17 grand.

claims.claim: The model takes a flat percentage of the total claim.
claims.quote: So, their revenue, you know, monetization or their model is they take a flat percentage of the total claim.

claims.claim: Alex gives an example of a $10% fee producing $800 on an $8,000 claim.
claims.quote: But in your example of they go get you even if it's eight, they'll take 10%. So they'll make 800 bucks.

claims.claim: In the example, the customer nets $7,200 and gains $2,200 over the initial offer.
claims.quote: Yeah, you netted 7,200. You still made $2,200 more than you would have by not hiring this person.

claims.claim: Alex says the franchise costs $43,000.
claims.quote: Their franchise cost for this is 43,000.

claims.claim: Alex says borrowing could reduce the cash needed to about $5,000.
claims.quote: So if you borrow money to do this, you might only need five grand to get started.

claims.claim: Alex reports average revenue of $2.6 million per person and a possible starting cost of $5,000 to $10,000.
claims.quote: they've got a bunch of existing operators, and their average revenue is $2.6 million per person off of a business that might have cost 5 to 10 grand to get started.

claims.claim: Alex reports gross margins of 70% to 90%.
claims.quote: Yeah, so typical gross margin, because it's such a low overhead business, is 70 to upwards of 90%

claims.claim: Alex reports net margins of 25% to 45%.
claims.quote: you can net 25 to, you know, 45% of that revenue.

claims.claim: The host speculates that profit could reach $700,000 to $800,000.
claims.quote: I mean, let's say, yeah, like 700 grand profit, 800 grand?

claims.claim: Alex says operators may take a few years to ramp up.
claims.quote: Yeah, that mean a few years to ramp, for sure.

acquisition_channels.details: Alex says the franchise provides leads and AI- and data-driven marketing tools.

ideas.delivery: The franchisee works with claimants and negotiates with insurers, using the franchisor's training, brand, leads and tools; licensing may be required.

prices: About $5,000 cash to start with borrowing

ideas.other_uk_rules: This is a US model. Before offering it in the UK, check FCA regulatory permissions and the UK claims-management and insurance-claims regulatory perimeter.

idea.name: Home preparation and improvement for sale
idea.one_liner: Coordinate repairs, cleaning, staging and small renovations for home sellers to improve sale prospects and value.
idea.customer: Home sellers, often referred by real-estate agents
idea.offer: Project-manage pre-sale home improvements through subcontractors
idea.revenue_model: Charge for project work; pricing may be fixed or tied to incremental value

key_quotes.quote: They help you as a home buyer, or sorry, as a home seller prep your house for selling it

claims.claim: Customers may pay $5,000 to $15,000 for improvements and preparation, with a claimed return of two to three times that amount in sale value.
claims.quote: You'll pay them 5 to 15 grand to do this, but you'll likely get two to three x that back in the form of what you sell your your home for.

claims.claim: The guest says the franchise investment is under $150,000, with a low end of $110,000.
claims.quote: So, I like that as a business because it's again smart, low to get into, less than 150k, and the low end is 110k.

claims.claim: The guest says borrowing could mean $10,000 to $15,000 to get started.
claims.quote: So, if you borrow money, again, you're into it for 10 to 15 grand and the average revenue of this business is 2.7 million dollars a year.

claims.claim: The guest reports average annual revenue of $2.7 million.
claims.quote: So, if you borrow money, again, you're into it for 10 to 15 grand and the average revenue of this business is 2.7 million dollars a year.

claims.claim: The host calculates that $2.7 million at a $15,000 average ticket would mean about 180 customers.
claims.quote: You divide it by 15,000, which could be their average ticket price, and that's 180 customers, which is like one closing every two days.

claims.claim: The host estimates a local operator would need about 8,000 annual home sales in the market and roughly 2% share to reach $2.7 million.
claims.quote: So in order to make 2.7 million with this franchise in this one city, not like all of North Dallas-Fort Worth, but this one suburb, you'd have to sell like 2% 2% of those homes sold per year.

claims.claim: The host's illustrative local-market calculation uses 40,000 homes, a five-year average stay and 8,000 annual sales.
claims.quote: 40,000 homes, let's say they live in them 5 years on average, so divide that by five, 8,000 homes are sold every year here in like a modestly sized suburb city.

claims.claim: The guest says some clients may spend $30,000 to $40,000 to seek $70,000 to $80,000 in added home value.
claims.quote: You know, some people are probably spending 30k, 40k with with this business to to make improvements to generate 70k and 80k in additional home value.

claims.claim: The host illustrates a $2,000 garage door potentially returning $4,000 in value.
claims.quote: So, like no one's really paying for it, the buyer isn't, the seller isn't, but the franchisee is is still making money cuz it's it's an investment and it's an investment you make at a time when you're about to make money.

claims.claim: The host gives a hypothetical example of a homeowner expecting $50,000 from a sale and needing $15,000 for improvements.
claims.quote: Cuz a lot of people, like even if they're about to make 50 grand on selling their home, and these improvements are going to cost 15 grand, they might not have that in their checking account, right?

claims.claim: The guest says gross margins range from 40% to 50%.
claims.quote: Yeah, so the gross margin for this business is anywhere from, you know, 40 to 50%.

claims.claim: The guest says net margins range from 12% to 22%.
claims.quote: Net margin is 12 to 22% depending on again how you're able to negotiate materials and the work from the subcontractors as well as the pricing structure with the seller.
